facts.name: Daylily
facts.notes: Tough, adaptable clumps of strappy leaves with a parade of lily-like flowers. Each flower lasts one day.
facts.toxSrc: ASPCA: toxic to cats (can cause kidney failure)

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Cutting Down Perennials in the Fall
sources.note: Cut peonies, daylilies, brunnera and speedwell in fall; cut bee balm and garden phlox with powdery mildew and destroy the leaves; rake up hosta leaves (slug eggs); cut yarrow and Shasta daisy flower stalks but keep the base leaves. Leave grasses, Siberian iris, baptisia, sedum, Joe-Pye weed, coneflower, black-eyed Susan and most natives standing; leave marginally hardy anise hyssop tops over winter; tidy hardy geraniums, heucheras, hellebores and moss phlox in spring.

companions.why: Combines well with beebalm and Shasta daisies; harmonizes with yellow foxglove, Coreopsis and lemon daylilies.

companions.why: Purdue Extension: interplant daffodils with late-emerging, sturdy perennials such as hosta, grasses or daylilies.
Purdue Extension: plant tulips with later-emerging plants that hide the ripening foliage, especially hosta, daylily and ornamental grasses.
Walters Gardens (Zeeland, Michigan) lists varieties of these as companions: yarrow, daylily, iris, catmint and sedum.
